Review Title: I lost more than $70,000 from my Wise…
Review Text:
I lost more than $70,000 from my Wise account in August 2022. That was my life savings. Years of work, gone in minutes, with no warning and no security check on activity that was completely unusual for my account.

Three years later I still have nothing back.

I want people to understand what this actually did. That money was not spare money. It was my security, my family's security, and every plan I had for my future. Since then every month has been shaped by a loss that was not my fault. I stopped being the person my family could rely on. I have spent three years writing letters and chasing deadlines instead of rebuilding my life.

Here is the part people should know.

When my case went to the Financial Ombudsman Service, Wise submitted documents as evidence. Those documents came from the person who took my money. Wise has now confirmed to me in writing, after the case was already decided against me, that this material came from the recipient of the funds and was never verified before it was submitted.

Think about what that means. Unverified documents supplied by the scammer were placed in front of the body deciding my case. I only found this out through a formal data protection request under UK GDPR, years later, and only after Wise missed multiple legal deadlines to answer me.

My money is gone. My account is closed. My case is closed. And the decision was made using material nobody checked.

I am not writing this out of anger alone. I am writing it because I have it in writing, and because anyone trusting Wise with their money deserves to know how a dispute can be handled when it goes wrong.

I have not forgotten. I am not going to.

Review Title: The “Cancel” button does NOT mean your…
Review Text:
The “Cancel” button does NOT mean your transfer is cancelled immediately

I am very disappointed with Wise’s cancellation process.

The interface gives the impression that cancelling a transfer is as simple as clicking “Cancel.” However, cancellation is apparently not immediate. I was informed that it can take up to two working days to process the cancellation.

That means the situation is very different from what the cancellation button suggests: you may click cancel, but your money can remain tied up for up to two working days while you wait for the cancellation to actually be completed.

This is a serious issue when dealing with money. If a customer decides they need to cancel a transfer, they may reasonably expect the cancellation to happen promptly and the funds to become available again. Instead, they can be left waiting for days.

I believe Wise should make this limitation clearly and prominently visible before the customer confirms the cancellation. A simple “Cancel” button without an obvious warning that the process may take up to two working days creates an impression of immediate cancellation that does not match the actual process.

Financial services should be transparent about when customers will regain access to their money. Two working days is not a minor detail — it can be financially significant.

Wise may provide a convenient transfer service, but the cancellation process needs much greater transparency. Customers should not have to discover only after clicking “Cancel” that their money may remain unavailable for up to two working days.

My advice to anyone using Wise: before sending a transfer, be aware that cancelling it may not be an immediate process, and your money may remain tied up while the cancellation is being processed.
